primitives.name: Muscular Contraction Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: But the diaphram itself is not seen, and consequently by no one who is not physiologically enlightened on the point is this diaphragm thought of in movement.
primitives.assumptions: Perceptual blindness to internal muscle dynamics; reliance on external chest expansion as proxy for diaphragm motion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when physiological reality contradicts visual intuition, leading to misinterpretation of contraction direction.

layer2.mapping: Maps internal muscle contractions to externally visible displacements in perceptual systems.
layer2.telemetry: Electromyography (EMG) recordings of diaphragm and rib muscle activity during respiration.

primitives.name: Motor Sensation Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: Now the curious point is thithat no sooner had I learned by the eye its objective spce-significance, than I found myself enabled mentally to f it as a movement upwards of a body in the situation of the uvula.
primitives.assumptions: Cross-modal integration between visual feedback and proprioceptive/motor imagery; ability to update internal models based on new sensory evidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Disruption happens when visual confirmation is delayed or absent, causing prolonged reliance on incorrect motor interpretations.

layer2.mapping: Translates explicit visual knowledge into implicit motor imagery, enabling accurate mental simulation of unseen movements.
layer2.telemetry: Functional MRI scans showing activation of premotor cortex during imagined versus observed swallowing motions.

primitives.name: Perceptual Bias Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: In a word, a muscular co traction gave me a sensation whereof I was unable durin forty years to interpret a motor meaning, of which two glances of the eye made me permanently the master.
primitives.assumptions: Sensory data fusion operates under prior expectations; explicit instruction can override these priors, correcting perceptual biases.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Error emerges when corrective information is ignored or not integrated properly, leading to persistent misperception.

layer2.mapping: Applies Bayes' theorem to update posterior beliefs about muscle motion after receiving diagnostic visual evidence.
layer2.telemetry: Psychophysical threshold measurements comparing perceived vs. actual displacement of anatomical landmarks during respiration.

The 'Muscular Contraction Isomorphism' demonstrates that internal muscle dynamics generate sensations that are mapped onto external surfaces, creating a perceptual shortcut. This shortcut breaks down when visual feedback contradicts the assumed direction of motion, as seen in the diaphragm example. The 'Motor Sensation Mapping' primitive shows that explicit visual confirmation can retroactively correct long-held internal models, allowing accurate mental simulation of unseen movements. Together, these primitives highlight the brain's capacity to integrate diverse sensory inputs to construct coherent motor representations, even when some elements remain invisible.
